turns.patient_response: My primary care doctor urged me to come here after a routine department physical flagged some issues, but I'm really struggling with this. To be honest, I’m scared that if I start eating more, I’ll lose control and put on weight I can’t afford at my age and in my line of work.

symptom_reasoning.S045: The patient explicitly states they are scared of putting on weight if they start eating more, which directly indicates a fear of weight gain.

turns.patient_response: I severely limit what I eat and never have episodes of overeating or trying to get rid of it. Most days I just get by on a black coffee in the morning and maybe a small piece of chicken or an apple late at night. Sitting down to a full meal just feels like I'm breaking discipline, so I avoid it.

symptom_reasoning.S043: The patient describes severely restricting their food intake to just black coffee and a tiny amount of food daily, while actively avoiding full meals.
symptom_reasoning.S048: The patient explicitly states they never have episodes of trying to get rid of the food they eat.
symptom_reasoning.S049: The patient explicitly denies ever having episodes of overeating.

turns.patient_response: Yes, my recent department physical flagged my weight as being significantly low, and my pants are hanging off me so much that I've had to punch extra holes in my duty belt. Even so, I still feel this constant urge to tighten up even further to avoid getting sloppy on the job.

symptom_reasoning.S044: The patient states that a recent physical flagged their weight as significantly low and that their pants are hanging off them.
symptom_reasoning.S045: The patient expresses a constant urge to tighten up even further to avoid getting sloppy, demonstrating a fear of gaining weight or becoming out of shape despite being significantly underweight.
symptom_reasoning.S046: The patient's self-evaluation of their professional competence ('avoid getting sloppy on the job') is unduly influenced by their body weight and shape ('urge to tighten up even further').

turns.patient_response: When I look in the mirror, I don't see a skinny guy; I just see a gut and flabby arms that make me feel like a failure as a cop and as a man. Keeping that number on the scale from going up feels like the only thing I still have any real control over in my life.

symptom_reasoning.S042: The patient describes feeling like a failure as a cop and as a man, which reflects self-criticism and low self-esteem.
symptom_reasoning.S045: The patient's strong focus on keeping the number on the scale from going up indicates an obsession with preventing weight gain.
symptom_reasoning.S046: The patient experiences a distorted body image, seeing a gut and flabby arms instead of a skinny frame, and allows this perception of his body to dictate his self-worth as a man and professional.
